summary: Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1961–1969). He held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1974–2002), Koyasan University (~2002–2012), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).
Yellava Subbarayalu is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as a professor at Tamil University and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (attested 2015).

Yeshe Thubten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1947–1959) and under teachers including Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Trijang Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, and Zong Rinpoche. He taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977–1978) and UVA (~1980–1981).
Yeshe Thupten is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1982, he held positions at Middlebury College and as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia.

Yeshi Dhonden was a Tibetology specialist who studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. In 1961, he founded Men-Tsee-Khang, where he served as director from 1961 to 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner.

Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. She served as department head and dean at University of the West (~1996–2003) and was a visiting scholar at Harvard (2001–2002).

Yigal Bronner is an Indology scholar who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1994–1999) under Sheldon Pollock. He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2008).

Yijie Tang was a scholar in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1947–1951), where he served as professor (~1956–2014), and held a post at Stanford University (~1990–1991).

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University, under Yinke Chen, and at Harvard University. He was a professor at Peking University (~1952–1999).

Yin Shun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, under Taixu and Qingnian, and at Taisho University. He held teaching posts at Minnan, Wuchang, Fawang Buddhist Institute, and served as president of Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Ying-shih Yü was a scholar of Sinology, history, and philosophy who earned his PhD from Harvard (1955–1962). He held professorships at Harvard, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Yale University (1977–1987), and Princeton University (1987–2001).

Yingguang Qu was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School (~1905–1907) and under traditional teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Nona Hutuktu, Gangkar Rinpoche, and Bai Puren.

Yinke Chen was a scholar of Sinology, history, and linguistics who studied at institutions including Berlin and Harvard. He held professorships at Tsinghua University, Peking University, National Southwestern Associated University, and Sun Yat-sen University.
Yirmiyahu Yovel was a philosophy scholar who studied at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (completed by 2013) under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University, and Kyoto University (PhD), and was a professor of philosophy, Buddhism, and Japanese poetry at the University of Haifa (~1983–2003).

Yohei Kawajiri is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He has held appointments as a research associate and scholar at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013, 2022) and as a special research fellow at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).
Yoichi Fukuda is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
